Hi Sofia —

Congrats again on the renewal greenlight. Per our conversation last week, I’m attaching a short addendum that captures two requests we discussed:

1) Make EU the primary data residency for production (pinning model & KV caches to EU nodes).
2) Add an APAC warm-standby pool (burst capacity + failover routing) for peak traffic windows.

Operational asks / notes:
- Estimated capacity uplift: +40% token throughput across your user-facing endpoints; see attached Capacity-estimate-2028Q3.xlsx for line-item pricing.
- Migration window: we recommend a 48-hour staged cutover during a low-traffic weekend; we can run a canary on 10% of traffic for 72 hours first.
- SLA/availability: warm-standby will incur a small MAU/commit uplift and a separate standby license line on the contract.
- Security: EU residency will be implemented with customer-managed keys in KMS and we’ll restrict cross-region caching.

Attached: Data-Locality-Addendum-draft.pdf and Capacity-estimate-2028Q3.xlsx. I included Monica and Ben for ops and pricing detail.

Can you confirm if procurement wants the addendum as a standalone DocuSign or folded into the renewal SOW? If you prefer, I can send a one-click DocuSign link.

Looking for a quick yes/no on the approach and any hard constraints on migration weekend availability (dates) from your side.

Thanks,
Sean

Folks —

Operational notes for the proposed plan:
- Canary plan: route 10% traffic to EU-primary nodes for 72 hours; if error rate <= 0.5% and 95th latency within 1.2x baseline, proceed to 48h staged cutover for remaining traffic.
- Rollback path: re-route traffic to global pool and invalidate client-side sticky sessions (we’ll provide a script). Full rollback SLA target: 2 hours from detection to restore baseline routing.
- KV cache movement: do not migrate hot KV entries; rehydrate gradually over 7 days post-cutover to avoid cold-token storms.
- APAC warm-standby: keep nodes in warm mode with preloaded model shards and disabled auto-batch until failover trigger. This reduces burst cost but increases standby commit by ~15%.

We should include a short SOW change that calls out the migration playbook, rollback SLAs, and acceptance criteria. I’ve attached SOW-diff-2028-04.pdf that highlights minimal edits.

Proposed dates: canary start 2028-05-28, cutover weekend 2028-06-08 to 2028-06-10 (flexible).

Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
